title: JOY
mv: You will show me the path of life; In Your presence is fullness of joy; At Your right hand are pleasures forevermore.
mvp: “You will show me the path of life; In Your presence is fullness of joy; At Your right hand are pleasures forevermore.” Psalm 16:11 (NKJV)
outline: Reasons Believers Must Live In Joy
assignment: Write out five (5) joy-building activities to practice daily this week e.g. gratitude journaling, worship, prayer walk, etc. (2X5=10 marks).

b.x: Everyone on earth desires to have joy. Yet, only a few people actually experience it. Joy is more than a feeling; it is a spiritual force rooted in God’s nature. Unlike happiness, which depends on circumstances, joy is birthed from the Holy Spirit and sustained by our relationship with Christ (Galatians 5:22). True joy shines brightest not in comfort, but in trials.

sections.h: REASONS BELIEVERS MUST LIVE IN JOY

i: Joy is a kingdom priority: The kingdom of God is characterised by “righteousness, peace, and joy in the Holy Spirit” (Romans 14:17). It is not optional but part of our spiritual identity.
It strengthens the Believer: Joy fortifies our hearts, sustains endurance, and fuels spiritual resilience. Where joy is lacking, strength diminishes (Nehemiah 8:10).
It glorifies God: Jesus wants our joy to be full (John 15:11). A joyful believer reflects Christ’s life, attracts others to the gospel, and testifies about the sufficiency of God’s grace.
It is a witness in trials: Joy in trials is evidence of spiritual maturity and trust in God’s sovereignty (James 1:2-3).
It flows from salvation: Joy springs from the awareness that we are redeemed, forgiven, and eternally secure (Psalm 51:12).

b.x: We develop joy through intimate fellowship with Jesus. When we remain connected to Him, His joy flows into our hearts (John 15:4-5, 11). This joy increases when we intentionally recall God’s goodness (1 Thessalonians 5:16-18). God’s word is a wellspring of joy; our perspective is renewed, and our spirit lifted when we constantly meditate on His word (Psalm 119:111). Casting our burdens on the Lord through prayer rather than carrying them ourselves is another way to live in perpetual joy (Philippians 4:6-7). Joy multiplies when we shift focus from self to others. Acts of love and service bring fulfilment (Acts 20:35; John 13:17). Joy is a fruit of the Spirit. As we yield daily to the Spirit’s leading, He produces abiding joy within us (Galatians 5:22; Romans 15:13).
Ultimate joy is realised when we see Jesus in Heaven (Psalm 16:11; Revelation 21:4).
